opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text: Our operating expenses are broadly classified as either compensation and benefits or non-compensation expenses. Expenses are recorded on the condensed consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss) when accrued, inclusive of expenses subsequently reimbursed by clients in accordance with ASC 606.

costs.heading: Operating Expenses
costs.text: Our operating expenses are broadly classified as either compensation and benefits or non-compensation expenses. Expenses are recorded on the condensed consolidated statements of comprehensive income (loss) when accrued, inclusive of expenses subsequently reimbursed by clients in accordance with ASC 606.

other_opex.text: Our non-compensation expenses include costs for rent and occupancy of our leased office spaces, travel and related expenses, professional services and development, technology and information services, depreciation and amortization, and other operating expenses. The majority of our non-compensation expenses fluctuate in response to changes in headcount.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense), Net
nonop.text: Other income (expense), net includes interest income earned on cash and cash equivalents and investment securities, and interest expense, commitment fees, and amortization of debt issuance costs on borrowings under our Credit Facilities.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text: We account for income taxes in accordance with ASC 740, Income Taxes (“ASC 740”). Because we are a holding company whose principal asset is an interest in LILP, a portion of our pre-tax earnings is attributable to noncontrolling interests and is not subject to federal, state or local income taxes at the Company level, which we expect to result in an effective tax rate below the statutory rate. Prior to the IPO, LILP was not subject to U.S. federal income tax and each partner was individually liable for taxes on its share of LILP’s income or loss, and accordingly the effective tax rates for periods prior to the IPO are not comparable to subsequent periods. See the section entitled “ Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates ” included in the Prospectus for a more detailed discussion of our income tax accounting.

In connection with the IPO, we also entered into a Tax Receivable Agreement that allocates some of the tax benefits of LILP for Class A common stock to the exchanging holder. Finally, our GAAP compensation expense changed following the IPO, as this cost is now recorded on our condensed consolidated statement of comprehensive income (loss) as compensation and benefits. Additionally, as a public company, we are subject to U.S. federal income taxes, which are recorded on our financial statements.

net sales.heading: Client Revenues
net sales.text: We generate client revenues primarily from advisory services provided under individually negotiated engagement letters that set forth our fee structure. Revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers, generally when the performance obligation set forth in the engagement letter has been satisfied. The amount and timing of fees we recognize can vary based on the type of engagement. We follow specific guidelines to ensure that our revenue is recognized in accordance with ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers. In general, revenue is recognized when the performance obligation outlined in the engagement letter has been satisfied.

Investment Banking Advisory.text:
R evenue trends in Investment Banking Advisory are generally correlated to the total volume and size of investment banking transactions completed. However, fluctuations from this trend may occur in any given year for any number of reasons, including but not limited to, changes in our market share or the ability of our clients to close transactions on which we have been engaged and are owed contingent fees. These events can cause our revenues to diverge from the level of overall volume of investment banking transactions completed.

Valuations and Opinions.text:
Revenue trends in Valuations and Opinions reflect two primary components: non-transaction-based services and transaction-based services. Non-transaction-based services are recurring portfolio valuations that are required by our valuation clients for financial reporting and regulatory purposes. The transaction-based services are primarily influenced by the overall market for U.S. announced M&A and financing transactions in a given year. Transaction based services include fairness opinions, solvency opinions, dispute advisory, and other transaction-based opinions and advisory services.

intro.text: Lincoln International, Inc. (NYSE: LCLN) is a trusted investment banking advisor to business owners, private equity firms and their portfolio companies, and public and private companies worldwide. Our services include mergers and acquisitions advisory, private funds and capital markets advisory, and valuations and opinions. With more than 1,400 professionals in more than 30 offices across 14 countries, we combine perspective on the global private capital markets with deep industry expertise, market intelligence and strategic insights to deliver exceptional execution and build lasting client relationships. We periodically provide other information for investors on the Investor Relations section of our website at www.lcln.com. We intend to use our website as a means of disclosing material non-public information and for complying with our disclosure obligations under Regulation FD.
